findings.title: Batch authorization checks only the first payment
findings.problem: The tenant authorization check examines only payments[0], but the subsequent loop refunds every captured payment returned by the repository.
findings.reason: A caller can submit a batch whose first resolved payment belongs to the actor and whose later payment belongs to another tenant. The first check passes, and the later captured payment is sent to record_refund without any tenant validation, creating a cross-tenant refund authorization bypass.
findings.suggestion: Validate payment.tenant_id against actor.tenant_id for every payment before recording any refund. Prefer validating the entire batch first so an invalid entry cannot leave a partially processed batch.

security.public_safe_summary: Batch authorization checks only the first payment

findings.title: Refund idempotency keys now collide across tenants
findings.problem: The repository idempotency key no longer includes actor.tenant_id even though repository keys use a global namespace and payment IDs are only unique within a tenant.
findings.reason: Two tenants using the same client idempotency key for payments with the same tenant-local payment ID produce an identical repository key. The repository can therefore treat one tenant's refund as the other tenant's retry, suppressing or misattributing a legitimate refund across tenants.

findings.title: Timestamp-only cursor cannot paginate rows sharing a timestamp
findings.problem: The next cursor records only the last row's created_at value, discarding the payment ID that breaks ties in the declared ordering.
findings.reason: When more than one page of rows shares the same created_at, the cursor cannot represent which row within that timestamp was last returned. A subsequent timestamp-only page_before call must either exclude remaining equal-timestamp rows or include already returned rows, causing omissions, duplicates, or a non-advancing page.
findings.suggestion: Keep both created_at and payment_id in Cursor and pass the composite cursor to page_before so the continuation predicate matches the (created_at DESC, id DESC) ordering.
